purpose: The file set the forge-live-write exercise compiles and runs, published as a tracked file so a gate can recompute it and measure the intersection required by docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 4, G6b, instead of accepting an argument about which edits were harmless. It follows .agents/v2/evidence/artifacts/V2-075-live-exercise-files.json exactly, with this task's exercising package and test name substituted; V2-075's artifact is not edited.
unexecuted_reason: external-unavailable: an owner-designated forge repository that may receive a reversible agent-written branch; needs: designate <owner>/<name> for the forge-write gate, or create a dedicated sandbox repository. The write target was NOT supplied, so no publication reached any real forge and this record claims no live observation. observed_commit above is the commit the file set was computed at, not the commit of a live observation: there is none. When the owner designates a target, the exercise must be run and this artifact re-measured, and its observed_commit becomes the observation commit at that point.

exercise.subtest_note: The exercise is one flat test with no subtests: it produces exactly one branch, so splitting it would either produce more than one branch or share mutable state between subtests. The gate behaviours were measured on this tree: with the gate unset the test SKIPS and logs its reason, and with the gate set and the designation absent it FAILS naming the missing designation.

measured_gate_behaviour.recorded_as: a measured failure naming the missing designation, not a skip

compiled.how: Every package of module github.com/takushi/agentic-loop-foundation/v2 reported by `go list -deps -test ./internal/runner`, contributing GoFiles, CgoFiles and EmbedFiles only. TestGoFiles and XTestGoFiles are deliberately NOT added per package: go list reports the test-augmented variant `internal/runner [internal/runner.test]` with its in-package test files already folded into that variant's GoFiles, so taking GoFiles alone yields exactly what the test binary compiles and does not wrongly pull in dependency packages' own test files, which the binary never compiles. The one entry go list reports that is not a repository file, the generated _testmain.go under the go build cache, is dropped by intersecting with `git ls-files`; a git diff can only ever name tracked paths, so that intersection loses nothing.

toolchain_pins.how: Files that fix what the compiled set is compiled and run with: go.mod and go.sum fix the module graph and the Go language and toolchain version, devbox.json and devbox.lock fix the Go toolchain binary and the shell the exercise runs inside. The Makefile is not in the set because this exercise is invoked as `go test` directly and no make target reaches it. All four are prohibited paths for this task and are byte-identical.

runtime_read.how: This exercise opens NO repository file while running. It reads three environment variables, creates a bare origin and a workspace under the test's own temporary directory, and reaches the forge only through the resolved absolute CLI. Measured by reading the test body: there is no os.ReadFile, no os.Open and no embedded path in TestForgePublicationLive, and the only repository files any test in this package reads are the two workflow files, which a DIFFERENT test reads and which are therefore already in the compiled-plus-tracked intersection as .github/workflows entries only if git ls-files names them -- it does not add them here because this exercise does not read them.

out_of_tree_executables.why_not_a_repository_path: The git binary is provided by the devbox environment outside the repository tree, so it can never appear in a git diff. Its identity is pinned instead by devbox.json and devbox.lock, both in the toolchain_pins group, and the adapter refuses any executable that is not an absolute path whose basename is the expected tool and which stats to a regular file.

The namespace helper is provided by the devbox environment outside the repository tree. It is pinned by devbox.json and devbox.lock, and NamespaceConfinement.Probe is a functional check rather than a version guess, so a kernel or a build that cannot provide the namespace fails the exercise instead of silently running it unconfined.

The forge CLI lives outside the repository, so it can never appear in a git diff and cannot be covered by the intersection at all. Measured on this machine: it is ABSENT from the validated `devbox run --pure` PATH and present at the conventional system location, which is why absolute path resolution through resolveTool is required rather than defensive. Its identity is checked before any process could exist: the path must be absolute, its basename must equal the expected tool and it must stat to a non-directory. This executable was NOT started by this task: the live leg is unexecuted.

excluded_with_reason.reason: These are the artefacts the observation writes rather than inputs it reads: this record and its index entry land after the exercise, so including them would make the G6b claim unsatisfiable for any live record whatsoever. Excluding them is not a gap in coverage. The evidence ledger's integrity is re-executed at the judging commit rather than argued about: `make check` runs `go test ./internal/contracts`, whose ledger tests re-check the index-to-file bijection and every evidence_hash. That is freshness by re-execution, which is G6a.
